_README: Occurrences of client-exposed secret-looking variables (NEXT_PUBLIC_*, VITE_*)
that are tolerated for now. Checked by .github/scripts/check-client-secrets.py,
which runs as part of the Code Review SOP Check on every PR.
An entry here is a tombstone, not a permission slip. Every entry must say why,
must expire within 90 days, and must match a line that actually exists — when
the line goes, the check fails until the entry goes with it.
Adding an entry needs the same CTO review as any other change under .github/
(see CODEOWNERS). If you are adding one to unblock yourself, that is the signal
to source the value server-side instead.
Everything currently listed is Security Tasklist item #2. Tracked in
docs/md/CyberSecurity/Client-Side Seed Material — Plan.md. The three env-template
entries expire sooner than the code entry because deleting a line from a template
is a same-week change, while removing the derivation is Phase 1.

allowed.reason: deriveKEK() derives the key protecting every user's RSA private key from userId + this variable + a constant salt. userId is not secret and a NEXT_PUBLIC_ value is published in the bundle, so the derived key is public. The backup flow in keys.ts is wired; it is inert only because the variable is unset and deriveKEK throws without it. Allowlisted so this check can land now and catch NEW occurrences. Fix is Phase 1 of the plan: move KEK derivation server-side onto the existing E2EE_SERVER_SECRET and delete this read.

Active template entry with the placeholder 'change-me-in-your-local-env' under a heading reading 'E2E backup KEK seed', plus the instruction to keep the value consistent across environments where recovery is expected. That instruction is what would cause someone to set this in production. Delete the entry and the comment block. Env-template changes to this file must target dev-main per sop-check Section 8.

Empty is why nothing is exposed today, but its presence in the production template is an instruction to populate it during provisioning. Delete the entry and the comment block. Changes to this file must target live-mvp per sop-check Section 8.
